artists.biography:
Tears for Fears are an English rock band formed in 1981 by Roland Orzabal and Curt Smith.
Founded after the dissolution of their first band, the mod-influenced Graduate, they were initially associated with the New Wave synthesizer bands of the early 1980s but later branched out into mainstream rock and pop, which led to international chart success.
Their platinum-selling debut album, The Hurting, reached number one on the UK Album Chart, while their second album, Songs from the Big Chair, reached number one on the U.S. Billboard 200, achieving multi-platinum status in both the UK and the United States. Following the release of their third platinum-selling album, The Seeds of Love (1989), Smith and Orzabal parted company in 1991, though Orzabal retained the Tears for Fears name throughout the remainder of the 1990s. The duo re-formed in 2000, and released an album of new material, Everybody Loves a Happy Ending, in 2004. To date, Tears for Fears have sold over 25 million albums worldwide, including more than 8 million in the U.S.

perplexity.description:
The Hurting, released on 7 March 1983 by Mercury Records, is the debut album of English band Tears for Fears. Musically, it blends electronic and pop styles with a strong synthpop and new wave influence, characterized by atmospheric synthesizers and introspective lyrics. The album explores dark themes such as child abuse, psychological trauma, and depression, making it a conceptually cohesive work despite its pop sensibility.

In the band's discography, The Hurting established Tears for Fears' signature sound and introduced their first major hits, including "Mad World," "Change," and "Pale Shelter," all of which reached the UK top five. Produced by Chris Hughes and Ross Cullum in close collaboration with band members Roland Orzabal and Curt Smith, the album was both a critical and commercial success. It peaked at number one on the UK Albums Chart shortly after release and was certified Platinum in the UK by 1985. Although initial reviews were mixed, the album has since gained retrospective acclaim for its emotional depth and production quality.
